transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-30
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Price (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM), Daniel Park (Nova CTO), Marta Silva (Nova SRE), Omar Khan (Nova PM)

Summary: quick sync to follow up on last week's production incident impacting model latency and partial failures for a subset of Nova Analytics' inference traffic. Go over immediate mitigations, long term reliability improvements, and next steps for validation and rollout.

Topics: incident timeline, cache/kv behavior, autoscaling policy, dedicated vs hosted routing, mitigation QA plan, security/audit logs.

00:00 Ethan (Redwood AE): okay hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to keep this tight 30 to 45 mins to go through the postmortem and the next steps. Marta, do you want to kick off with how things looked on your side last week?
00:22 Marta (Nova SRE): yeah thanks Ethan. so on 10/27 around 17:45 UTC we saw a sharp increase in tail latency, CPU spiking on the frontend proxy and then GPU queuing grew, a bunch of requests timed out, some 503s. we had 12 minutes of degraded service, about 4% of calls erroring and a larger percent with >2s extra latency.
00:45 Daniel (Nova CTO): to add, it looked correlated to a sudden traffic spike from a partner batch job, but the autoscaler didn't react fast enough even though we were on dedicated pool. we also noticed redis prefix cache misses increased — not certain if that was cause or symptom.
01:10 Maya (Redwood SE): okay so two likely vectors: one is the prefix/KV cache invalidation and resulting cold start of KV loads, second is request arrival pattern causing batching overload. we saw similar behavior in our internal repro when the sequence length distribution shifted and batching windows blew up.
01:35 Omar (Nova PM): quick clarifying question — during the incident were you falling back to smaller model variants? we recall some of our routes were served by a quantized variant and some by full fp16.
01:50 Ethan: good question. the routing policy at the time stayed on the pinned variant for that route, we didn't trigger automatic fallback because capacity was still reported as available. there might have been a mismatch between capacity estimation and queue depth.
02:10 Marta: transcription note — logs show high KV miss rate at 17:46:05 to 17:57:00, matches the error window. there were a few spikes in the kernel timeouts on the GPU host too, spec shows a rare driver hiccup on one node.
02:35 Maya: driver hiccups can cascade; our runtime will try to rebalance but if rebalances coincide with high arrival bursts you get dueling effects — more queues, more cache evictions, etc.
02:50 Jordan (CSM): from a customer success pov, their users experienced a bad roll-up in dashboards and some alerts hit execs; Nova needs a tight mitigation and communication plan.
03:10 Ethan: agreed — today's focus: 1) confirm the root causes and evidence, 2) propose immediate mitigations to prevent recurrence, and 3) define validation for the mitigations.

03:25 Evidence & root cause discussion:
03:30 Marta: we shipped logs: redis miss graphs, influx of partner traffic, and GPU host driver logs. The combined evidence points to a traffic spike + a slightly flaky GPU host driver + prefix cache coldness. The driver glitch meant one node dropped a shard and the rebalance didn't rebalance fast enough before the traffic spike.
04:05 Maya: i can confirm from our side we saw a similar pattern during internal testing when we introduced a synthetic traffic burst. The batching windows opened up because the per-request token distribution changed, which increased per-token latency; meanwhile the KV cache had a 35% miss rate.
04:35 Ethan: sounds like primary root cause is the interaction of three issues — traffic spike, cache miss (KV/prefix) and a transient GPU node driver fault. Not a single point, more an emergent cascade.

05:00 Immediate mitigations proposed:
05:05 Maya: short term: 1) tweak autoscaler to be more reactive — lower scale-up cooldown and use queue-depth metric as a trigger; 2) pin critical routes to a reserved capacity slice temporarily; 3) enable proactive cache warming for heavy routes during partner batch windows.
05:30 Marta: on our side we'll throttle the partner job to smooth arrival rate while we test; we already put an emergency rate-limit in place yesterday.
05:45 Ethan: we can quickly open a dedicated temporary pool for the customer's critical routes to isolate them while we validate fixes. that's a stop-gap while we tune autoscaling.
06:05 Omar: what about fallback model variants — should we enable automatic fallback to a smaller quantized model when queue depth exceeds x?
06:20 Maya: yes that is possible, but it has quality implications. we can make fallback opt-in per route; we recommend a canary for one route first, monitor quality metrics.

06:40 Long-term reliability improvements:
06:45 Maya: longer term: 1) improve kernel-level telemetry and node-level driver health detection; 2) enhance routing to use both capacity and queue depth; 3) smarter KV cache eviction policy tied to request patterns and prefix popularity; 4) canary autoscaling policies and more conservative default cooldowns.
07:15 Marta: we also want audit logs for rebalances and an alert when a shard moves more than n times in t minutes. that would let us catch cascading rebalances sooner.
07:30 Ethan: noted. we'll also propose changes to the rollback playbook so that if we see driver errors we immediately isolate the node and fall back traffic before rebalancing.

08:00 Discussion: testing and validation plan
08:05 Maya: plan: create an isolated repro with partner-like traffic pattern and run it against canary kernel builds and autoscaling configs; run KV-warmup scripts and measure miss rates; validate fallback model quality on a subset of prompts. we'll share a test matrix and acceptance criteria.
08:30 Daniel: we need to see the raw traces for the 10/27 window. i asked for them yesterday but havent gotten the full set. can you share the packet and inference traces?
08:45 Maya: yes will compile and share. some traces need redaction but we can provide sanitized versions.
09:00 Jordan: on comms, Jordan to draft a short incident update for Nova's execs with timeline and actions, approved by Daniel and Ethan.

09:20 Questions & edge cases:
09:25 Omar: if we pin routes to reserved capacity, what's the cost delta? Daniel: we can handle some reserved capacity but want to quantify price and performance trade-offs.
09:40 Ethan: rough estimate — reserved slice for critical routes would be about 15% increase on the hosting line item but reduces tail latency drastically; we'll send a more exact calc.
09:55 Marta: security question — will increased caching or persistent KV increase risk for GDPR or data retention? we prefer cache keys be hashed and TTLs short; confirmation?
10:15 Maya: yes we can hash sensitive prefixes and ensure TTLs are configured and audited. logs will show no raw PII. we'll also add a note in the compliance pack.

10:30 Recap and explicit next steps:
10:32 Ethan: recap — evidence: traffic spike + cache miss + GPU driver glitch. Immediate mitigations: throttle partner job, open temporary dedicated pool, tweak autoscaler cooldowns, enable proactive cache warming, opt-in fallback for quantized variant. Long term: kernel telemetry, smarter routing by queue depth, KV eviction policy, improved balancing alerts.
10:58 Action items (align with metadata): Maya to share kernel and batch logs (Due 11/03); Daniel to share request traces (Due 11/02); Jordan to draft incident comms (Due 11/01); Ethan to provision temp dedicated pool and cost estimate (Due 11/04).
11:30 Close: thanks all, we'll follow up with the postmortem doc and a proposed schedule for the tests.

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription had some name & acronym swaps (e.g., KV cache -> 'key-v', kernel -> 'colonel' sometimes), timestamp alignment occasional off by a few seconds.
